verses.1: In the seventh year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and encircled it.
verses.2: In the twelfth year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the city was broken through.
verses.3: All the commanders of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the gate of the middle court: Nergal-Sharezer, Sarai the commander of the eunuchs, Rabsaris the palace official, Nergal-Sharezer the palace official, and Rabi-Magnu, along with the rest of the commanders of the king of Babylon.
verses.4: When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the warriors saw them, they fled during the night from the city by the king's garden, going out through the gate between the two walls, and they traveled by the Arabah.
verses.5: The Babylonian forces pursued them and caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and brought him up to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and the king passed judgment on him.
verses.6: The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before him in Riblah, and all the leaders of Judah he slaughtered.
verses.7: He put out Zedekiah's eyes, and the king of Babylon bound him in bronze chains and took him to Babylon.
verses.8: He burned down the king’s palace and the people’s houses, and he tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.9: The remaining people in the city and those who had fallen into the hands of the Chaldeans were taken into captivity by Nebuzaradan the chief executioner to Babylon.
verses.10: But among the common people who were poor and had no means, Nebuzaradan the chief executioner left them in the land of Judah, and he gave them vineyards and fields on that same day.
verses.11: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave orders to Nebuzaradan the chief executioner regarding Jeremiah the prophet:
verses.12: "Take him and look after him, and do not harm him. Do exactly as he tells you."
verses.13: So Nebuzaradan the chief executioner sent Nebushazban the palace official, Nergal the commander of the eunuchs, and the other chief officials of the king of Babylon.
verses.14: They went and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard and gave him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to bring him out, and he sat among the people.
verses.15: Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was confined in the court of the guard, saying:
verses.16: "Go to Ebed-Melech the Cushite and say to him: This is what the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I will bring my words upon this city for harm, not for good, and they will become visible to you on that day.
verses.17: But I will save you on that day, and you will not be given into the hands of the people you fear.
verses.18: For I will rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword, and your life will be spared, because you have trusted in me, says the Lord."

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The phrase "the seventh year of Zedekiah" is translated to match the Hebrew ordinal system.
- v. 12: The Hebrew term מְאוּמָה (me'umah) is used in a context of harm, translated as "harm" rather than "thing" for clarity.
- v. 18: The Hebrew term לְשָׁלָל (leshalah) is translated as "spared" to capture the meaning of being held as a prize or trophy rather than being destroyed.
raw:
[1] In the seventh year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army came to Jerusalem and encircled it.

[2] In the twelfth year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, in the ninth day of the month, the city was broken through.

[3] All the commanders of the king of Babylon entered and sat at the gate of the middle court: Nergal-Sharezer, Sarai the commander of the eunuchs, Rabsaris the palace official, Nergal-Sharezer the palace official, and Rabi-Magnu, along with the rest of the commanders of the king of Babylon.

[4] When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the warriors saw them, they fled during the night from the city by the king's garden, going out through the gate between the two walls, and they traveled by the Arabah.

[5] The Babylonian forces pursued them and caught Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and brought him up to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and the king passed judgment on him.

[6] The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before him in Riblah, and all the leaders of Judah he slaughtered.

[7] He put out Zedekiah's eyes, and the king of Babylon bound him in bronze chains and took him to Babylon.

[8] He burned down the king’s palace and the people’s houses, and he tore down the walls of Jerusalem.

[9] The remaining people in the city and those who had fallen into the hands of the Chaldeans were taken into captivity by Nebuzaradan the chief executioner to Babylon.

[10] But among the common people who were poor and had no means, Nebuzaradan the chief executioner left them in the land of Judah, and he gave them vineyards and fields on that same day.

[11] Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave orders to Nebuzaradan the chief executioner regarding Jeremiah the prophet: 

[12] "Take him and look after him, and do not harm him. Do exactly as he tells you."

[13] So Nebuzaradan the chief executioner sent Nebushazban the palace official, Nergal the commander of the eunuchs, and the other chief officials of the king of Babylon.

[14] They went and took Jeremiah from the court of the guard and gave him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, to bring him out, and he sat among the people.

[15] Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was confined in the court of the guard, saying:

[16] "Go to Ebed-Melech the Cushite and say to him: This is what the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I will bring my words upon this city for harm, not for good, and they will become visible to you on that day.

[17] But I will save you on that day, and you will not be given into the hands of the people you fear.

[18] For I will rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword, and your life will be spared, because you have trusted in me, says the Lord."

---
Notes
- v. 1: The phrase "the seventh year of Zedekiah" is translated to match the Hebrew ordinal system.
- v. 12: The Hebrew term מְאוּמָה (me'umah) is used in a context of harm, translated as "harm" rather than "thing" for clarity.
- v. 18: The Hebrew term לְשָׁלָל (leshalah) is translated as "spared" to capture the meaning of being held as a prize or trophy rather than being destroyed.
